passed_checks.claim: All five home-page profiles returned HTTP 200 and remained on https://chatgpt.com/.
No horizontal document overflow was detected in any profile or round.
Under the Android mobile user-agent at 412x915, sidebar, login, attachment, dictation and send controls exposed 44x44 CSS-pixel boxes.
At 412x520, the signed-out composer and suggestion CTA remained visible without horizontal overflow. A real virtual keyboard was not opened.
The mobile login page displayed provider choices, email input, Continue and Try it first without horizontal overflow; primary provider and Continue controls were 340x44 CSS pixels.
No console or page runtime error was recorded on the public home page in either mobile-UA mobile round.
Observed CLS ranged from 0 to 0.0004 across the public profiles.

observations.claim: At the same 412x915 viewport, desktop and Android mobile user-agents received materially different signed-out home variants.

evidence.desktop_ua_header: Sidebar + ChatGPT model selector + Log in

observations.impact: This confirms a separate mobile-web delivery branch. It is not a defect by itself, but fixes and experiments must be validated on both branches rather than inferred from viewport-only testing.

observations.claim: Six POST requests under /unauth-mweb/events/ were recorded as net::ERR_ABORTED in both rounds for each mobile-UA home profile.
observations.adjudication: The endpoints are event/telemetry routes and the evidence was captured around bounded page teardown. No visible user failure, missing content or HTTP error response was observed. Do not report as a product defect without a lifecycle experiment that proves loss before teardown.

observations.claim: The mobile login page emitted one opaque console error represented as JSHandle@error in both rounds.
observations.adjudication: The current logger did not preserve the error object and no visible login-state failure was established. A focused diagnostic run must serialize console arguments before any defect claim.

observations.claim: The generic 44-pixel detector flagged the textarea content box, the 36-pixel-high suggestion CTA and legal links.
observations.adjudication: The composer has a larger 54-pixel form container and the critical icon buttons are 44x44. The standalone suggestion and legal links require standards-aware spacing/context review; the raw count must not be reported as an accessibility failure.

observations.claim: The geometry detector reported composer overlap with a fixed/sticky container.
observations.adjudication: Screenshots show the composer is not obscured. The detected container is an ancestor layout surface that naturally contains the composer. The detector must exclude ancestor/descendant pairs.

observations.claim: A text-only public fetch suggested repeated start-state wording.
observations.adjudication: The browser matrix found no duplicate visible heading in any profile. Do not report the text-only signal as a defect.

unknowns: Real virtual-keyboard resize, safe-area and browser-chrome interaction.
Authenticated long-chat scrolling, streaming and return-to-latest behaviour.
Attachments, camera, image/file preview and permission recovery.
Search sources, widgets, Projects, Work, custom GPTs and plan-limit states.
TalkBack, browser zoom, external keyboard and switch-control behaviour.
The detailed object behind the repeated login-page JSHandle@error.
Whether mobile event POST aborts occur before lifecycle teardown or lose required analytics.
recommended_next_tests: Run a focused login console probe that serializes console argument values and stacks without submitting credentials.
Run pagehide/visibilitychange/beforeunload lifecycle timing for /unauth-mweb/events/ to distinguish expected teardown aborts from premature loss.
Run an authorised mobile account matrix for long chat, streaming, sidebar history, attachment tray and offline recovery.
Run a real Android Chrome session with virtual keyboard and visualViewport tracing.
Run TalkBack and 200% browser zoom task checks on the primary composer and login path.
verdict_meaning: The public mobile web passes the basic route, overflow, compact-height and primary-control checks. Preserve the distinct mobile delivery branch and run focused diagnostics for two user-impact-unknown signals before any external defect report.
